*Bringing necessary packages into current session*

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(rsample)
```

## PART ONE: CHECKING THE DATA

*Reading in data*

```{r}
seoul_bike_data <- read_csv('SeoulBikeData.csv', locale = locale(encoding = 'Latin1'))
```

*Checking for missing values*

```{r}
is.na(seoul_bike_data)
#No NAs!
```

*Checking column types and values within columns*

```{r}
#Checking column types
str(seoul_bike_data)

#Checking summary statistics
num_summaries <- seoul_bike_data |>
  select(`Temperature(°C)`, `Humidity(%)`, `Wind speed (m/s)`, `Visibility (10m)`, `Dew point temperature(°C)`, `Solar Radiation (MJ/m2)`, `Rainfall(mm)`, `Snowfall (cm)`, `Rented Bike Count`, Hour)

summary(num_summaries)

#Checking categorical variable unique values
unique(seoul_bike_data$Seasons)
unique(seoul_bike_data$Holiday)
unique(seoul_bike_data$`Functioning Day`)
```

*Changing **Date** data*

```{r}
#Date is stored in a day/month/year format as a character
seoul_bike_data_new <- seoul_bike_data |>
  mutate(Date = dmy(Date))

str(seoul_bike_data_new$Date)
```

*Changing characters into factors*

```{r}
seoul_bike_data_cat <- seoul_bike_data_new |>
  mutate(
    Seasons = as.factor(Seasons),
    Holiday = as.factor(Holiday),
    `Functioning Day` = as.factor(`Functioning Day`)
  )
str(seoul_bike_data_cat$Seasons)
str(seoul_bike_data_cat$Holiday)
str(seoul_bike_data_cat$`Functioning Day`)
```

*Renaming all variables*

```{r}
seoul_bike_data_final <- seoul_bike_data_cat |>
  rename(date = Date, rented_bike_count = `Rented Bike Count`, hour = Hour, temp = `Temperature(°C)`, humidity = `Humidity(%)`, windspeed = `Wind speed (m/s)`, visibility = `Visibility (10m)`, dew_point_temp = `Dew point temperature(°C)`, solar_rad = `Solar Radiation (MJ/m2)`, rainfall = `Rainfall(mm)`, snowfall = `Snowfall (cm)`, seasons = Seasons, holiday = Holiday, fun_day = `Functioning Day`)

str(seoul_bike_data_final)
```

*Creating summary statistics*

```{r}
#Calculating mean, sd, and median for bike rentals
seoul_bike_data_final |>
  summarize(mean_rent = mean(seoul_bike_data_final$rented_bike_count), med_rent = median(seoul_bike_data_final$rented_bike_count), sd_rent = sd(seoul_bike_data_final$rented_bike_count))

seoul_bike_data_final |>
  group_by(seasons) |>
  summarize(mean_rent = mean(seoul_bike_data_final$rented_bike_count), med_rent = median(seoul_bike_data_final$rented_bike_count), sd_rent = sd(seoul_bike_data_final$rented_bike_count))

seoul_bike_data_final |>
  group_by(holiday) |>
  summarize(mean_rent = mean(seoul_bike_data_final$rented_bike_count), med_rent = median(seoul_bike_data_final$rented_bike_count), sd_rent = sd(seoul_bike_data_final$rented_bike_count))

seoul_bike_data_final |>
  group_by(fun_day) |>
  summarize(mean_rent = mean(seoul_bike_data_final$rented_bike_count), med_rent = median(seoul_bike_data_final$rented_bike_count), sd_rent = sd(seoul_bike_data_final$rented_bike_count))

#Filtering out days that were not functioning
new_bike_data <- seoul_bike_data_final |>
  filter(fun_day != 'No')

new_bike_data$fun_day
```

*Summarizing daily data*

```{r}
#Getting all of the means and sums for the numeric variables
day_bike_data <- new_bike_data |>
  group_by(date, seasons, holiday) |>
  summarize(
    bike_sum = sum(rented_bike_count),
    rain_sum = sum(rainfall),
    snow_sum = sum(snowfall),
    mean_hum = mean(humidity),
    mean_temp = mean(temp),
    mean_wind = mean(windspeed),
    mean_dew = mean(dew_point_temp),
    mean_solar = mean(solar_rad),
    mean_vis = mean(visibility),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

str(day_bike_data)
```

*Recreating summary stats*

~Summaries~

```{r}
#Finding mean, median, and standard deviation for bike_sum, with the last two being across the seasons and holiday categories
day_bike_data |>
  summarize(mean_bike = mean(bike_sum), med_bike = median(bike_sum), sd_bike = sd(bike_sum))

day_bike_data |>
  group_by(seasons) |>
  summarize(mean_bike = mean(bike_sum), med_bike = median(bike_sum), sd_bike = sd(bike_sum))

day_bike_data |>
  group_by(holiday) |>
  summarize(mean_bike = mean(bike_sum), med_bike = median(bike_sum), sd_bike = sd(bike_sum))

```

~Plots~

```{r}
#Making a heatmap to analyze the density of bike rentals depending both on if it was a holiday and the season
ggplot(day_bike_data |>
         drop_na(seasons, holiday, bike_sum), aes(x = seasons, y = holiday, fill = bike_sum)) +
  geom_tile(color = 'white') +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = 'white', high = 'red') +
  labs(title = "Analysis of Density of Bike Rentals by 'Holiday' and 'Seasons' Categories", x = 'Seasons', y = 'Holiday', fill = '# of Bike Rentals')
```

```{r}
#Making a scatterplot to see if there are more or less bike rentals depending on the amount of rainfall
ggplot(day_bike_data |>
         drop_na(bike_sum, rain_sum), aes(x = bike_sum, y = rain_sum)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = 'Analysis of Relationship Between Bike Rentals and Rainfall', x = '# of Bike Rentals', y = 'Rainfall')
```

```{r}
#Making another scatterplot to see if there are more or less bike rentals depending on the amount of snowfall
ggplot(day_bike_data |>
         drop_na(bike_sum, snow_sum), aes(x = bike_sum, y = snow_sum)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = 'Analysis of Relationship Between Bike Rentals and Snowfall', x = '# of Bike Rentals', y = 'Snowfall')
```

```{r}
#Making line graph that compares bike rentals with dew point temperature
ggplot(day_bike_data |>
         drop_na(bike_sum, mean_dew), aes(x = mean_dew, y = bike_sum)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = 'Analysis of Bike Rentals and Dew Point Temperature', x = 'Dew Point Temperature', y = '# of Bike Rentals')
```

~Correlations~

```{r}
#Calling all numeric variables
correlations <- day_bike_data |>
  select(rain_sum, snow_sum, mean_hum, mean_temp, mean_wind, mean_dew, mean_solar, mean_vis)

#Finding correlations between the bike_sum variable and all other numeric variables
cor(day_bike_data$bike_sum, correlations)
```

## PART TWO: SPLIT THE DATA

```{r}
#Splitting data
split_data <- rsample::initial_split(day_bike_data, prop = 0.75, strata = seasons)
split_data

#Naming split sets
training_split <- training(split_data)
test_split <- testing(split_data)
```

## PART THREE: FITTING MLR MODELS

*Creating **weekend/weekday** variables in the training and test sets*

```{r}
#Creating weekend_or_weekday variable for training set
split_data_train <- training_split |>
  mutate(weekend_or_weekday = factor(if_else(wday(date) %in% c(1,7), 'weekend', 'weekday')))

#Creating weekend_or_weekday variable for test set
split_data_test <- test_split |>
  mutate(weekend_or_weekday = factor(if_else(wday(date) %in% c(1,7), 'weekend', 'weekday')))

split_data_train
split_data_test
```

*Creating standardized versions of numeric variables*

```{r}
#Creating a vector with all numeric variables
numeric_vars <- c('mean_hum', 'mean_temp', 'mean_wind', 'mean_dew', 'mean_solar', 'mean_vis', 'rain_sum', 'snow_sum')

#Finding mean for all numeric variables
num_mean <- split_data_train |>
  summarize(across(all_of(numeric_vars), mean))

num_mean

#Finding standard deviation for all numeric variables
num_sd <- split_data_train |>
  summarize(across(all_of(numeric_vars), sd))

num_sd

#Creating standardized versions of all numeric variables
for(v in numeric_vars){
  split_data_train[[paste0(v,'_standardized')]] <- 
    (split_data_train[[v]] - num_mean[[v]]) / num_sd[[v]]
  
  split_data_test[[paste0(v, '_standardized')]] <-
    (split_data_test[[v]] - num_mean[[v]]) / num_sd[[v]]
}


mean(split_data_train$snow_sum_standardized)
sd(split_data_train$snow_sum_standardized)
```

*Fitting first model*

```{r}
#This model includes all standardized numeric variables as well as seasons, holiday, and the weekend_or_weekday variable created earlier
model_1 <- lm(
  bike_sum ~ mean_temp_standardized + mean_hum_standardized + mean_wind_standardized + mean_dew_standardized + mean_solar_standardized + mean_vis_standardized + rain_sum_standardized + snow_sum_standardized + seasons + holiday + weekend_or_weekday,
  data = split_data_train
)
```

*Fitting second model*

```{r}
#This model uses the same variables as model_1 but includes interactions between seasons and holiday, seasons and mean temperature, and mean temperature and the rain sum
model_2 <- lm(
  bike_sum ~ mean_temp_standardized + mean_hum_standardized + mean_wind_standardized + mean_dew_standardized + mean_solar_standardized + mean_vis_standardized + rain_sum_standardized + snow_sum_standardized + seasons + holiday + weekend_or_weekday + seasons * holiday + seasons * mean_temp_standardized + mean_temp_standardized * rain_sum_standardized,
  data = split_data_train
)
```

*Fitting third model*

```{r}
#This model takes everything from model_2 and adds squared terms for temperature and humidity
model_3 <- lm(
  bike_sum ~ mean_temp_standardized + mean_hum_standardized + mean_wind_standardized + mean_dew_standardized + mean_solar_standardized + mean_vis_standardized + rain_sum_standardized + snow_sum_standardized + seasons + holiday + weekend_or_weekday + seasons * holiday + seasons * mean_temp_standardized + mean_temp_standardized * rain_sum_standardized + I(mean_temp_standardized^2) + I(mean_hum_standardized^2),
  data = split_data_train
)
```

*Finding the RMSE*

```{r}
#Making an 'rmse' function that can be used on the models
rmse <- function(actual, predicted){
  sqrt(mean((actual - predicted)^2))
}

#Using predict
model_1_pred <- predict(model_1, newdata = split_data_test)
model_2_pred <- predict(model_2, newdata = split_data_test)
model_3_pred <- predict(model_3, newdata = split_data_test)

#Using 'rmse' to find the best fit model and putting the results into a tibble
test_all <- tibble(
  model = c('Model 1', 'Model 2', 'Model 3'),
  rmse_result = c(
    rmse(split_data_test$bike_sum, model_1_pred),
    rmse(split_data_test$bike_sum, model_2_pred),
    rmse(split_data_test$bike_sum, model_3_pred)
  )
)

test_all
```

*Fitting the best model to the entire data set (model_3 is the one we want to use for this because it has the lowest RMSE!)*

```{r}
#Reproducing the standardization and alterations to the data set
final_data <- day_bike_data |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(weekend_or_weekday = factor(if_else(wday(date) %in% c(1,7), 'weekend', 'weekday')))

final_mean <- final_data|>
  summarize(across(all_of(numeric_vars), mean))

final_sd <- final_data |>
  summarize(across(all_of(numeric_vars), sd))

for(v in numeric_vars){
  final_data[[paste0(v,'_standardized')]] <- 
    (final_data[[v]] - final_mean[[v]]) / final_sd[[v]]
}

#Creating final model for full data
final_model <- lm(
  bike_sum ~ mean_temp_standardized + mean_hum_standardized + mean_wind_standardized + mean_dew_standardized + mean_solar_standardized + mean_vis_standardized + rain_sum_standardized + snow_sum_standardized + seasons + holiday + weekend_or_weekday + seasons * holiday + seasons * mean_temp_standardized + mean_temp_standardized * rain_sum_standardized + I(mean_temp_standardized^2) + I(mean_hum_standardized^2),
  data = final_data
)

#Reporting coefficients in a tibble
final_tibble <- tibble(coef(final_model)) |>
  arrange(desc(coef(final_model)))

final_tibble
```
